## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite source data on the cell $A\mathbb Z^3$
from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$,
integers $M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ whose signed representatives are
injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and satisfy $|k_r|<M_r/2$. Require $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$, and let $c_k=4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}/(V|\kappa_k|^2)$ be the positive Ewald coefficient. Use the assignment factors $a_k,b_k,\rho_k,z_k$ of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], and put $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$.

For a query point $x$ write $t=A^{-1}x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^3$ and define the retained exact and mesh reciprocal potentials by
$$U_{\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\rho_k\overline{a_k(t)}),\qquad U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(z_k\overline{b_k(t)}).$$
Define $E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2$ and $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$. For each mode let $A_k$ be the source-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]], and let $B_k$ be the derivative-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-derivative-window-alias-bound]].

Let a complex-vector derivative/gather value $d_k(t)$ satisfy $\|d_k(t)-\mathfrak d_k(t)\|_2\le H_k$ for a stated $H_k\ge0$, where $\mathfrak d_k$ is the declared derivative branch of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]] and $\nabla_x=A^{-T}\nabla_t$. The uncorrected mesh and exact reciprocal forces are
$$F^d_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{z_k}d_k(t_i)),\qquad F_{\mathcal K,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\rho_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
Then for every query point $x$,
$$|U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)-U_{\mathcal K}(x)|\le Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),\qquad |E_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),$$
and for every particle $i$,
$$\|F^d_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k\bigr].$$

For the declared energy-gradient gather $d_k=\mathfrak d_k$ (so $H_k=0$), the mesh force is $-\nabla_{x_i}E_{M,\mathcal K}$ wherever the classical derivative exists. This holds everywhere for $P\ge3$ and off the assignment knots for $P=2$; at a $P=2$ knot the selected one-sided derivative or its average is a procedure value, with the same bound but without a differentiability claim.

The optional diagonal self correction is
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k(|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}=E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M.$$
For its finite cyclic implementation, set $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on $\mathcal K$,
$$\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r},\qquad S_i=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Then $\gamma$ is real and even, $S_i=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|b_k(t_i)|^2$, and, on every differentiable branch (or as the same declared one-sided branch at a $P=2$ knot),
$$\nabla_{x_i}(S_i/2)=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Consequently this local cyclic-kernel expression computes $C_M$ and its derivative exactly in real arithmetic.
The finite tensor-transform gathers also have the exact real-arithmetic forms
$$U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_x)u_\ell,\qquad u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_kz_k}{D(k)}e^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i),\qquad \lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_k\overline{z_k}}{\overline{D(k)}}e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}.$$
These identities hold with the declared derivative branch, including the selected one-sided $P=2$ knot value.
It satisfies
$$|E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k).$$
In the energy-gradient branch its exactly differentiated force is
$$F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\overline{z_k-q_ib_k(t_i)}\,\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\bigr),$$
and
$$\|F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k\bigr].$$
The corrected force is the classical gradient in the same differentiable cases; at a $P=2$ knot it is only the declared branch value. No pointwise error estimate here replaces an RMS estimate, and no claim is made that a different spectral differentiation rule is the gradient of the mesh energy.

1.3 The mode sums are finite. For $P\ge3$, and for $P=2$ off the assignment knots, [F4] supplies the classical derivatives. Since $z_k=\sum_jq_jb_k(t_j)$ by [F3], [F7] gives $
abla_{x_i}z_k=q_i
abla_xb_k(t_i)$. Differentiating $ rac12c_k|z_k|^2$ yields $q_ic_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{z_k}
abla_xb_k(t_i))$, so negating and summing proves $F^
abla_{M,i}=-
abla_{x_i}E_{M,\mathcal K}$ in those differentiable cases. Also $
abla_{x_i}ho_k=q_i
abla_xa_k(t_i)$ by [F5]; differentiating $ rac12c_k|ho_k|^2$ gives $q_ic_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{ho_k}
abla_xa_k(t_i))$, so the negative derivative is exactly $F_{\mathcal K,i}$. At a $P=2$ knot the chosen derivative is a procedure value, not a classical derivative. [F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, algebra]

## Statement

At an AAA iteration with Loewner matrix $L\in\mathbb C^{(N-m)\times m}$,
the selected unit weight vector $w$ minimizes $\|Lv\|_2$ among all
$v\in\mathbb C^m$ with $\|v\|_2=1$; its residual is the smallest singular
value of $L$. If every selected weight is nonzero and the iteration does not
return pole status, its barycentric candidate interpolates all selected
support data. The finite support budget makes the procedure terminate after
at most $B$ iterations. These claims concern finite sampled data and do not
assert minimax optimality or uniform off-grid convergence.

1.2 The right singular subspace $E$ is nonzero. If every projection $P_Ee_j$ of a coordinate basis vector vanished, then every vector of $E$ would be orthogonal to every coordinate basis vector and hence would be zero, a contradiction. Thus the least index with nonzero projection exists; the normalization and phase convention in [F1] choose a unique unit vector in $E$, also when the smallest singular value is repeated or zero. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

## Statement

At an AAA iteration with Loewner matrix $L\in\mathbb C^{(N-m)\times m}$,
the selected unit weight vector $w$ minimizes $\|Lv\|_2$ among all
$v\in\mathbb C^m$ with $\|v\|_2=1$; its residual is the smallest singular
value of $L$. If every selected weight is nonzero and the iteration does not
return pole status, its barycentric candidate interpolates all selected
support data. The finite support budget makes the procedure terminate after
at most $B$ iterations. These claims concern finite sampled data and do not
assert minimax optimality or uniform off-grid convergence.

1.1 Let $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ be a full orthonormal right singular-vector basis for $L$, with singular values $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_m\ge0$ and $\sigma_m=\sigma_{\min}(L)$. Hence $\|Lw\|_2=\sigma_{\min}(L)$ and no unit vector gives a smaller Loewner residual. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

## Statement

On every nondegenerate triangle, a point lies in the triangle if and only if its unique barycentric coordinates are all nonnegative; these coordinates also give the unique affine interpolant matching the three vertex data. Interpolants on adjacent triangles with common vertex data agree on their shared face. On an edge, the interpolant is the degree-one cardinal polynomial interpolant. For every nonempty finite site set, the nearest-site query returns a minimizer, breaks ties by least identifier, and reports correctly whether the query is inside or outside the convex hull.

1.1 The matrix with columns $p_1-p_0,p_2-p_0$ is invertible by [A1], so the two coordinate equations uniquely determine $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ and then $\lambda_0=1-\lambda_1-\lambda_2$. Thus the coordinates in [F1] are unique, and their nonnegativity is exactly membership in the convex combinations defining the triangle. [given, F1, A1, algebra]

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Input $a<b$, an integer $n\ge1$, exponents $\alpha,\beta>-1$, nonnegative integers $m_a,m_b$, a function $h\in C^{2n}([a,b])$ in the sense of [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]], and positive integers $q_a,q_b$ satisfying $q_a(\alpha+1)-1>2n$ and $q_b(\beta+1)-1>2n$. On $(a,b)$ define

## Statement

For $p>0$, $P,C\in\mathbb R^3$, and $\eta=pq/(p+q)$ with $p,q>0$, the Hermite Coulomb auxiliaries of [[def-hermite-gaussian-coulomb-auxiliary-functions]] satisfy
$$R^n_{000}(p,P-C)=(-2p)^nF_n(p\|P-C\|^2),$$
$$R^n_{t+1,u,v}=(P_1-C_1)R^{n+1}_{tuv}+tR^{n+1}_{t-1,u,v},$$
with the corresponding coordinate formulas for increasing $u$ or $v$ and with negative-index terms zero. The one-center and two-center base Coulomb integrals are
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{e^{-p\|x-P\|^2}}{\|x-C\|}\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{p}F_0(p\|P-C\|^2),$$
$$\int\!\!\int\frac{e^{-p\|x-P\|^2}e^{-q\|y-Q\|^2}}{\|x-y\|}\,dy\,dx=\frac{2\pi^{5/2}}{pq\sqrt{p+q}}F_0(\eta\|P-Q\|^2).$$
For a primitive pair expansion $g_ag_b=\sum_{tuv}E_{ab}^{tuv}\Lambda_{tuv}$, the nuclear attraction integral is
$$V_C(g_a,g_b)=\frac{2\pi}{p}\sum_{tuv}E_{ab}^{tuv}R^0_{tuv}(p,P-C).$$
For two primitive pairs, with coefficients $E_{ab}$ and $E_{cd}$ and centers $P,Q$, the Coulomb integral is
$$G(g_a,g_b;g_c,g_d)=\frac{2\pi^{5/2}}{pq\sqrt{p+q}}\sum_{tuv}\sum_{\tau\nu\phi}\overline{E_{ab}^{tuv}}E_{cd}^{\tau\nu\phi}(-1)^{\tau+\nu+\phi}R^0_{t+\tau,u+\nu,v+\phi}(\eta,P-Q).$$
All sums are finite; the largest Boys order is bounded by the total polynomial degree in the participating primitives.

1.1 For $r>0$, the Gaussian integral and substitution $u=sr$ give $r^{-1}=(2/\sqrt\pi)\int_0^\infty e^{-s^2r^2}ds$. Insert this representation into the one-center integral; Tonelli applies to the nonnegative integrand. Completing the square in $x$ using [F1] gives a three-dimensional Gaussian integral $(\pi/(p+s^2))^{3/2}$ times $e^{-ps^2\|P-C\|^2/(p+s^2)}$. The substitution $t=s/\sqrt{p+s^2}$ maps $[0,\infty)$ monotonically onto $[0,1)$ and simplifies the remaining factor to $2\pi/p\int_0^1e^{-p\|P-C\|^2t^2}dt$, which is the stated base formula. [given, F1, F5, F7, L8, algebra]

For $p>0$, $P,C\in\mathbb R^3$, and $\eta=pq/(p+q)$ with $p,q>0$, the Hermite Coulomb auxiliaries of [[def-hermite-gaussian-coulomb-auxiliary-functions]] satisfy
$$R^n_{000}(p,P-C)=(-2p)^nF_n(p\|P-C\|^2),$$
$$R^n_{t+1,u,v}=(P_1-C_1)R^{n+1}_{tuv}+tR^{n+1}_{t-1,u,v},$$
with the corresponding coordinate formulas for increasing $u$ or $v$ and with negative-index terms zero. The one-center and two-center base Coulomb integrals are
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{e^{-p\|x-P\|^2}}{\|x-C\|}\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{p}F_0(p\|P-C\|^2),$$
$$\int\!\!\int\frac{e^{-p\|x-P\|^2}e^{-q\|y-Q\|^2}}{\|x-y\|}\,dy\,dx=\frac{2\pi^{5/2}}{pq\sqrt{p+q}}F_0(\eta\|P-Q\|^2).$$

## Example

For Burgers' flux $f(u)=u^2/2$ and entropy $\eta(u)=u^2/2$, the entropy flux
is $q(u)=u^3/3$ and the entropy potential is $\psi(u)=u^3/6$. The symmetric
two-point flux
$$f^{ec}(u_L,u_R)=\frac{u_L^2+u_Lu_R+u_R^2}{6}$$
is entropy-conservative. Adding unit dissipation in entropy variables gives
$f^{es}=f^{ec}-(u_R-u_L)/2$; at the jump $1\to0$ its Tadmor entropy residual
is exactly $-1/2$.
1.1 Here $\eta''(u)=1$, $\eta'(u)=u$, and $q'(u)=u^2=\eta'(u)f'(u)$, so this is a convex entropy pair. Thus $v=u$ and $\psi=uf-q=u^3/6$ by [F1]. [given, F1, algebra]

## Statement

Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite periodic matching affine simplicial mesh, write $V_K=\int_K1\,dx>0$ for its cell volumes, let $\beta$ be constant, and let $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be convex. Assume the cellwise forward-Euler condition in [[thm-pe04-first-order-upwind-forward-euler-conservation-and-entropy]] holds for $\Delta t$, including its Countable Choice premise through the affine-simplex Green formula. For the autonomous degree-zero upwind DG ODE, write $E_{\Delta t}(U)=U+\Delta t L_h(U)$. The exact SSPRK(3,3) recurrence is
$$Y_1=E_{\Delta t}(U^n),\qquad Y_2=\frac34U^n+\frac14E_{\Delta t}(Y_1),\qquad U^{n+1}=\frac13U^n+\frac23E_{\Delta t}(Y_2).$$
Then $\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^{n+1})\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^n)$. This guarantee is for the degree-zero scalar upwind operator just specified; it is not a fully discrete entropy theorem for the high-order nonlinear flux-differencing SBP method.

1.1 By [F1], the spatially autonomous SSPRK(3,3) step has exactly the three displayed convex-combination stages. Set $C=\mathbb R^{\mathcal T_h}$ and $\Phi(U)=\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K)$. For $U,V\in C$ and $0\le t\le1$, apply [F5] in each cell and multiply by $V_K>0$ from [F6]; summing proves convexity of $\Phi$. [given, F1, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite periodic matching affine simplicial mesh, write $V_K=\int_K1\,dx>0$ for its cell volumes, let $\beta$ be constant, and let $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be convex. Assume the cellwise forward-Euler condition in [[thm-pe04-first-order-upwind-forward-euler-conservation-and-entropy]] holds for $\Delta t$, including its Countable Choice premise through the affine-simplex Green formula. For the autonomous degree-zero upwind DG ODE, write $E_{\Delta t}(U)=U+\Delta t L_h(U)$. The exact SSPRK(3,3) recurrence is
$$Y_1=E_{\Delta t}(U^n),\qquad Y_2=\frac34U^n+\frac14E_{\Delta t}(Y_1),\qquad U^{n+1}=\frac13U^n+\frac23E_{\Delta t}(Y_2).$$
Then $\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^{n+1})\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^n)$. This guarantee is for the degree-zero scalar upwind operator just specified; it is not a fully discrete entropy theorem for the high-order nonlinear flux-differencing SBP method.

1.1 By [F1], the spatially autonomous SSPRK(3,3) step has exactly the three displayed convex-combination stages. Set $C=\mathbb R^{\mathcal T_h}$ and $\Phi(U)=\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K)$. For $U,V\in C$ and $0\le t\le1$, apply [F5] in each cell and multiply by $V_K>0$ from [F6]; summing proves convexity of $\Phi$. [given, F1, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron. Then
$$\{u\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega):\operatorname{curl}u=0\}=\nabla H_0^1(\Omega).$$
The gradient range is closed in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $\|q\|_{H^1}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla q\|_2$ for $q\in H_0^1(\Omega)$. The boundary is connected as a consequence of these stated geometric hypotheses; it is not an extra assumption.

1.1 Let $u$ lie in the left-hand kernel and take $u=z+\nabla q$ from [F1]. Then $\operatorname{curl}z=0$. By [F2], $z=\nabla r$ for $r\in H^1(\Omega)$. Since each $z_j\in H^1$, its weak derivatives give all second derivatives of $r$, so $r\in H^2(\Omega)$. Extend $r$ by [F3] to $a\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$. This has a continuous representative: Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|\widehat a\|_1\le\|(1+|\xi|^2)\widehat a\|_2\|(1+|\xi|^2)^{-1}\|_2<\infty$ in dimension three, and its positive-sign inverse integral $g(x)$ is the reflection of the integral Fourier transform of $\widehat a$, hence continuous by [F4]. Its truncated integrals converge uniformly to $g$, since the error is bounded by the $L^1$ Fourier tail, which tends to zero by dominated convergence. They converge in $L^2$ to $a$ by [F4]. On every finite-measure ball the uniform convergence is also $L^2$ convergence, so uniqueness of the $L^2$ limit there shows $g=a$ almost everywhere. Smooth compactly supported approximants to $a$ converge in $H^2$ by [F4] and uniformly by the same Fourier bound applied to their differences; no unproved $L^1$ inversion assumption on $a$ is made. Consequently $r$ has a continuous representative on $\overline\Omega$. [F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra, F4]

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron. Then
$$\{u\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega):\operatorname{curl}u=0\}=\nabla H_0^1(\Omega).$$
The gradient range is closed in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $\|q\|_{H^1}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla q\|_2$ for $q\in H_0^1(\Omega)$. The boundary is connected as a consequence of these stated geometric hypotheses; it is not an extra assumption.

2.1 On any compact patch of the interior of a planar boundary face there is an inward rectangular slab of fixed height $b>0$ inside $\Omega$. For a smooth function on this slab, the one-dimensional fundamental theorem in the normal direction and Cauchy–Schwarz give $\|f|_{s=0}\|_{L^2(\text{patch})}^2\le \frac{2}{b}\|f\|_{L^2(\text{slab})}^2+2b\|\partial_s f\|_{L^2(\text{slab})}^2.$ This defines a bounded $H^1$ face restriction by smooth approximation: the already proved Lipschitz extension [F3] on a bounded rectangular slab, followed by the whole-space density theorem [F4] at $k=1$, gives the required dense smooth restrictions. Since $z\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, approximating by compactly supported smooth vector fields shows that the restriction of $z$ to this patch is zero. Approximate $a$ from step 1.1 in $H^2$ by the smooth functions of [F4]; their gradients converge in $H^1$ on the slab and their values converge uniformly. Thus the restriction of $r$ is its continuous face value and the tangential derivatives of that restriction are the restrictions of the tangential components of $\nabla r=z$: integrate the smooth tangential derivative identity against a compactly supported smooth test on the face and pass to the limit using the slab estimate. These derivatives are zero. By [F3] in dimension two, the continuous boundary value of $r$ is constant on each connected planar face interior. One may split disconnected faces into their finitely many polygonal components. Continuity makes those constants extend to their closures. Since the boundary is connected by [F2] and these finitely many closed faces cover it, its continuous image under $r$ is a connected subset of a finite set of constants, hence one constant $c$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra, F4]

## Statement

On $\Omega=(0,3)$ with homogeneous endpoint values, the $h=1$ centered
finite-difference discretization of the semilinear equation
$-u''+u^3=0$ has fine residual
$$F(u)=Au+(u_1^3,u_2^3),\qquad A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$
Use $P=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, $Iu=(u_1+u_2)/2$, $R=P^{\mathsf T}$, the
Galerkin coarse residual $F_H(v)=P^{\mathsf T}F(Pv)$, one pre- and one
post-sweep $S(u)=u-\tfrac14F(u)$, and the exact selected coarse root. The
unique fine root is $u_*=0$. The actual exact-branch FAS two-grid map is a
contraction toward $u_*$ on $\overline B_2(0,1/100)$ with error factor at most
$27/400$.

1.1 The continuous model is $-u''+u^3=0$ on $(0,3)$ with zero endpoint values, and this proof concerns the specified finite-difference residual. The vectors $(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$ and $(1,-1)^{\mathsf T}$ are eigenvectors of $A$ with eigenvalues $1$ and $3$, so $z^{\mathsf T}Az\ge\|z\|_2^2$. For real $s,t$, $(s-t)(s^3-t^3)=(s-t)^2(s^2+st+t^2)\ge0$, since $s^2+st+t^2=((2s+t)^2+3t^2)/4$. Therefore, for $a,b\in\mathbb R^2$, $\langle a-b,F(a)-F(b)\rangle=(a-b)^{\mathsf T}A(a-b)+\sum_{i=1}^2(a_i-b_i)(a_i^3-b_i^3)\ge\|a-b\|_2^2$. Since $F(0)=0$, any other root $a$ would give $0=\langle a,F(a)-F(0)\rangle\ge\|a\|_2^2$, so $u_*=0$ is the unique root. Direct differentiation gives $DF(0)=A$. [given, algebra]

## Statement

Consider one two-grid FAS cycle with fixed pre-smoothing result, exact selected
coarse root $v(u)$, prolongation $P$, and a post-smoother that is
$L_{\rm post}$-Lipschitz on the relevant corrected states. Suppose a coarse
solver returns $\widehat v$ with residual
$\eta=\|F_H(\widehat v)-g_H(u)\|_2$ and a separately verified
residual-to-solution estimate
$$\|\widehat v-v(u)\|_2\le M_H\eta.$$
Then the inexact-cycle output $\widehat E(u)$ and exact-cycle output $E(u)$
satisfy
$$\|\widehat E(u)-E(u)\|_2\le L_{\rm post}\|P\|_{\rm op}M_H\eta.$$
If the exact cycle satisfies the root-error estimate
$\|E(u)-u_*\|_2\le\kappa\|u-u_*\|_2$ on a stated invariant region, then
for every iteration input $u_k$ in that region whose exact and inexact
corrected states satisfy the preceding hypotheses,
$$\|u_{k+1}-u_*\|_2\le\kappa\|u_k-u_*\|_2+L_{\rm post}\|P\|_{\rm op}M_H\eta_k.$$
Invertibility of $DF_H$ alone is not asserted to imply the stated
residual-to-solution estimate; that bound must be proved under additional
coarse-operator hypotheses.

1.1 Let $z=u_{\rm pre}+P(v(u)-Iu_{\rm pre})$ and $\widehat z=u_{\rm pre}+P(\widehat v-Iu_{\rm pre})$ be the exact and inexact corrected states. By [F1], subtraction cancels $u_{\rm pre}$ and $Iu_{\rm pre}$, so $\widehat z-z=P(\widehat v-v(u))$. Hence [A1] gives $\|\widehat z-z\|_2\le\|P\|_{\rm op}\|\widehat v-v(u)\|_2\le\|P\|_{\rm op}M_H\eta.$ [F1, A1, algebra]

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with total mass $Q$. Let $\rho_\varepsilon=\eta_\varepsilon*\mu-Q/L^d$ and let $\phi_\varepsilon$ be its unique zero-mean periodic Poisson potential from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]]. Put $E_\varepsilon=-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon$. Use the shape and periodic centered-difference Poisson operator of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] and [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Let $s_h=P_h^\varepsilon\mu-Q/L^d$, let $A_h\phi_h=s_h$ with $\bar\phi_h=0$, set $E_{h,j}=-D^0\phi_h$, and gather $G_hE_h$ using the same shape. Define
$$ C_{\rm dep}=\frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV},\quad C_{\rm FD}=\frac1{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^4\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\quad C_{\rm src}=C_{\rm dep}+C_{\rm FD}, $$ where $C_\eta,Z_{\min}$ are from [[lem-periodic-pic-shape-partition-and-quadrature-bound]]. Put $$ C_3=\frac16\left(\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^3\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad C_{\rm int}=\frac{C_{\eta,E}+\|E_\varepsilon\|_\infty C_\eta}{Z_{\min}}, \quad C_{\eta,E}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\left|\partial_{y_a y_a}[\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)E_\varepsilon(y)]\right|_2 . $$ For vector fields, $\|V\|_\infty=\sup_x|V(x)|_2$ (the maximum of Euclidean lengths for grid fields); the derivatives in $C_{\eta,E}$ use this same Euclidean norm. Then the source $s_h$ is compatible and $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2}\left(\gamma_{N,L}C_{\rm src}+C_3\right) +C_{\rm int}h^2. $$
The displayed $\gamma_{N,L}$ is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm of [[thm-periodic-pic-poisson-residual-to-gathered-force-bound]] and satisfies $\gamma_{N,L}\le L/4$. Thus for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this fixed-$\varepsilon$ force error tends to zero as $h\to0$. Every constant depends on the stated smooth regularized solution and kernel; this is not an $\varepsilon\to0$ estimate.

1.1 The assigned source has mean zero: by the partition identity in [F1], $h^d\sum_j(P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j=\int\sum_jw_j(x)\,d\mu(x)=Q$, so subtracting the background gives zero mean. By [F4], the continuum potential and field are smooth; [F2] gives the unique grid potential. The assignment and centered-stencil Taylor bounds give the residual $r_h=s_h-A_h(\phi_\varepsilon|_h),\qquad \|r_h\|_\infty\le C_{\rm src}h^2 .$ Here [F1] bounds the measure-assignment error by $C_{\rm dep}h^2$, and for each coordinate the centered second difference has remainder at most $h^2\|\partial_a^4\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty/12$, whose sum is $C_{\rm FD}h^2$. [F1, F2, F4, given, algebra]

## Statement

Under the two inequalities in [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]],
every fixed-control row of its explicit update is an affine combination of the
center and the two coordinate neighbors with nonnegative coefficients summing
to one, plus $\tau f^a$. Therefore the max over controls is order-preserving.

## Statement

Assume the first-order HJB coefficients satisfy the hypotheses of
[[def-na-first-order-hjb-cauchy-problem]]. Under the CFL condition in
[[alg-na-upwind-hjb-grid-step]], each one-control update is a convex
combination of the current node and its one-sided neighbors plus
$\tau\ell_a$. Consequently the control-minimum update is order-preserving and
$$\|U^{n+1}\|_\infty\le\|U^n\|_\infty+\tau L.$$
For a smooth periodic test function $\phi$ with bounded derivatives through
order two, the normalized local residual satisfies
$$\frac{\phi(t_n+\tau,x_i)-S_{h,\tau}\phi(t_n,\cdot)_i}{\tau} =\phi_t(x_i,t_n)+H(x_i,t_n,D\phi(x_i,t_n))+O(\tau+h_{\max}+\eta_k(P)),$$
where $S_{h,\tau}$ is the scheme map, $h_{\max}=\max_jh_j$, $P$ bounds
$|D\phi|$ on the tested compact set, and $\eta_k(P)=0$ for exact control
minimization.

1.1 The CFL condition makes the center coefficient in [F1] nonnegative; all neighbor coefficients are nonnegative by $b_{a,j}^\pm\ge0$. Their sum is $$1-\tau\sum_j|b_{a,j}|/h_j+\tau\sum_j(b_{a,j}^++b_{a,j}^-)/h_j=1.$$ Thus each row is a convex combination of nodal values plus $\tau\ell_a$ and is order-preserving. A pointwise minimum of order-preserving maps is order-preserving. Every row value lies in $[-\|U^n\|_\infty-\tau L,\|U^n\|_\infty+\tau L]$, so the minimum has the same bound. [F1, given, algebra]

## Definition

Assume exact-real arithmetic in which each arithmetic operation, comparison,
square root, real power on a positive argument, scalar residual evaluation,
and call to the one-step Newton procedure terminates. **Inputs:**
admissible primitive states $(\rho_L,u_L,p_L)$ and $(\rho_R,u_R,p_R)$, gas
constant $\gamma>1$, pressure-width tolerance $\tau>0$, and iteration budget
$N\in\mathbb N_0$. **Outputs:** `inadmissible-input`, `vacuum`,
`pressure-bracket` with an interval, or `budget-exhausted` with an interval.
The procedure never treats a nonzero residual tolerance as an exact root.

1. If $\rho_L,\rho_R,p_L,p_R$ are not all positive or $\gamma\le1$, return
   `inadmissible-input` before evaluating a wave response.
2. Compute $\Phi(0+)$ from
   [[thm-euler-star-pressure-root-and-vacuum-criterion]]. If $\Phi(0+)\ge0$,
   return `vacuum`.
3. Otherwise set the bracket $[a,b]=[0,P]$ with $P$ from that theorem. Its
   endpoint convention is $\Phi(a):=\Phi(0+)<0<\Phi(b)$.
4. For at most $N$ iterations, in this order:
   1. If $b-a\le\tau$, return `pressure-bracket` with $[a,b]$.
   2. Let $m=(a+b)/2$. Call
      [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on the scalar residual
      $F(p)=\Phi(p)$ over the open domain $(0,\infty)$, starting at $m$, with
      residual tolerance $0$ and update budget $1$.
   3. If Newton returns $(r,\texttt{root})$, return `pressure-bracket` with
      $[r,r]$. If it
      returns `iteration-budget-exhausted` with last iterate $q$ and
      $a+(b-a)/4\le q\le b-(b-a)/4$, use $q$ as the query. In every other
      status or when this central-quarter test fails, use $m$ as the query.
   4. Evaluate $\Phi$ at the query. If it is zero, return `pressure-bracket`
      with the singleton interval. If negative, replace $a$ by the query; if
      positive, replace $b$ by the query.
5. After the budget, return `pressure-bracket` if the width is at most $\tau$;
   otherwise return `budget-exhausted` with the current bracket.

The returned interval uses the zero lower endpoint as a limiting endpoint, not
an admissible pressure. This algorithm gives a finite status and bracket; the
separate theorem below proves its invariant and width reduction. It makes no
claim that an exhausted budget found a root.

## Example

For $f(u)=u^2/2$ and $u_0(x)=1$ for $x<0$, $u_0(x)=0$ for $x>0$, the entropy shock moves right at speed $1/2$. For states $a,b\in[0,1]$, define the positive-state Burgers Godunov flux by $F_G(a,b)=\min_{v\in[a,b]}f(v)$ when $a\le b$ and $F_G(a,b)=\max_{v\in[b,a]}f(v)$ when $a>b$. Since $f$ is increasing on $[0,1]$, both cases give $F_G(a,b)=a^2/2$. Minmod slopes vanish for the initial step, so the first MUSCL flux update is the first-order Godunov update; the batch-29 monotone finite-volume theorem applies to its mesh-refined baseline under Countable Choice and the stated CFL conditions.

3.1 Define $u(t,x)=1$ for $x<t/2$ and $u(t,x)=0$ for $x>t/2$. The jump speed is $s=1/2=(f(1)-f(0))/(1-0)$, so [F5] gives the weak jump law. For $0\le k\le1$, the Kruzhkov entropy-flux jump is $q_k(0)-q_k(1)-\tfrac12(|0-k|-|1-k|)=k^2-k\le0$; for $k\le0$ and $k\ge1$ direct substitution gives zero. The initial trace is strong locally because the shock moves a distance $t/2\to0$. Hence [F4] identifies this profile as a bounded Kruzhkov solution; uniqueness in [F3] makes it the convergence target from step 2.1. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a polyhedral open set with a conforming affine simplicial mesh, let $K_+$ and $K_-$ share an interior facet $F$, and let $w\in H^1(D)$. The elementwise $L^2(F)$ traces of $w|_{K_+}$ and $w|_{K_-}$ agree almost everywhere on $F$.

1.1 Fix a compact $(d-1)$-simplex $G$ contained in the relative interior of $F$. A sufficiently small open tube around $G$ has closure in $D$. Cover its closure by finitely many balls whose larger concentric balls still have closure in $D$; [F2] supplies a smooth cutoff equal to one on each smaller ball and supported in its larger ball. The function $\chi=1-\prod_i(1-\chi_i)$ is compactly supported in $D$ and equals one near $G$. The zero extension $W$ of $\chi w$ belongs to $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$: for a test function $\psi$, the weak product rule follows directly from $\int_D\chi w\,\partial_i\psi=\int_Dw\,\partial_i(\chi\psi)-\int_Dw(\partial_i\chi)\psi=-\int_D(\chi\partial_iw+w\partial_i\chi)\psi,$ and compact support of $\chi$ removes any boundary term on extension. [A1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

## Example

Let $\Omega=\{(x,y,z):(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}-R)^2+z^2<r^2\}$ be a solid torus with $R>r>0$. Define
$$u(x,y,z)=\left(-\frac{y}{x^2+y^2},\frac{x}{x^2+y^2},0\right).$$
This is a smooth curl-free and divergence-free field on $\overline\Omega$, tangent to the boundary, whose circulation around the core circle is $2\pi$. Here “harmonic” means curl and divergence both vanish with zero normal boundary component. It is a concrete nonzero-period field caused by the handle; the nonzero period proves it is not the gradient of a single-valued $C^1$ potential. It is the continuous model for the nontrivial cohomology components described in [[thm-na-lowest-order-discrete-de-rham-cohomology-and-harmonic-modes]].

1.1 On $\overline\Omega$, $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\ge R-r>0$, so every component of $u$ and its first derivatives are bounded; hence $u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ and its classical curl is also in $L^2$. Direct differentiation by [F2] gives $\operatorname{div}u=2xy/(x^2+y^2)^2-2xy/(x^2+y^2)^2=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}u=0$. Thus [F1] places $u$ in H(curl) with zero curl. [A1, F1, F2, given, algebra]

cases.input_text: Degenerate simplices and zero-length edges are excluded by the affine tetrahedron and mesh hypotheses.
cases.reason: The large radius exceeds the tube radius, keeping the entire closed torus away from the axis where the field denominator vanishes.
cases.review_reason: The large radius exceeds the tube radius, keeping the entire closed torus away from the axis where the field denominator vanishes.

2.1 Write $e_\theta=(-\sin\theta,\cos\theta,0)$. On the torus boundary the normal is a linear combination of the meridional radial vector $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,0)$ and $e_3$, whereas $u=e_\theta/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; hence $u\cdot n=0$. Along the core curve, $u(\gamma(\theta))=e_\theta/R$ and $\gamma'(\theta)=R e_\theta$, so $\int_\gamma u\cdot d\ell=\int_0^{2\pi}1\,d\theta=2\pi$. A single-valued $C^1$ potential would have zero integral around every closed curve by [F4], so this field is not such a gradient and represents a nonzero period. This is the type of harmonic component retained by [F3]. [A1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice in the inherited edge/face finite-element space branch. Let $V=H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ with the PEC convention in [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]], and let $V_h=N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$. Define
$$m(u,v)=\int_\Omega v^T\epsilon u\,dx,\qquad a(u,v)=\int_\Omega (\operatorname{curl}v)^T\mu^{-1}\operatorname{curl}u\,dx,\qquad a_+(u,v)=m(u,v)+a(u,v).$$
For $u\in V$, the **Maxwell curl-energy Ritz projection** $R_hu\in V_h$ is the solution of
$$a_+(R_hu,v_h)=a_+(u,v_h)\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
Its finite-dimensional well-definedness, orthogonality, and best-approximation property are supplied by [[lem-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection-well-defined]].

$$m(u,v)=\int_\Omega v^T\epsilon u\,dx,\qquad a(u,v)=\int_\Omega (\operatorname{curl}v)^T\mu^{-1}\operatorname{curl}u\,dx,\qquad a_+(u,v)=m(u,v)+a(u,v).$$

## Statement

Assume AC and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. Let $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, let $P_N,K_N=P_NK_k,f_N=P_Nf$ and the exact cell-pair matrices be as in [[def-volume-product-integration-scheme]], and suppose $I-K_k$ is injective. Then there is $N_0$ such that for all $N\ge N_0$ the matrix $I-A^{(N)}$ is nonsingular and its reconstruction $u_N\in V_N$ is the unique solution of $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$. If $u\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ solves $(I-K_k)u=f$, then for a constant $C<\infty$ independent of $N$ and $f$,
$$\|u_N-u\|_2\le C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr).$$
Writing $C_F:=\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}/(4\pi)$, the exact far-field outputs obey
$$\|\mathcal F_k[u_N]-\mathcal F_k[u]\|_{C(S^2)}\le C_F C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr)\longrightarrow0.$$
This gives eventual solvability and convergence for the stated cell-volume product rule; it does not assert operator-norm convergence $K_N\to K_k$ or finite-precision error bounds.

1.1 Let $X=L^2(D;\mathbb C)$. Since $|D|>0$, $X\ne\{0\}$ (a normalized indicator of any positive-measure cell or subset is nonzero). By [F6] and AC, $X$ is a Banach space. [F2] gives compactness of $K_k$, and the assumed injectivity makes the Fredholm premise of [F3] applicable once the approximation hypotheses are checked. [F2, F3, F6, given]

2.1 Let $B_X$ be the closed unit ball and $C=\overline{K_k(B_X)}$. Compactness in [F2] makes $C$ compact. Strong convergence $P_Nz\to z$ from [F1] is uniform for $z\in C$: given $\epsilon>0$, cover $C$ by finitely many $\epsilon/3$ balls with centers $z_1,\ldots,z_s$, choose $N_0$ so that $\|P_Nz_j-z_j\|<\epsilon/3$ for every center and $N\ge N_0$, then use $\|P_N\|\le1$ to get $\sup_{z\in C}\|P_Nz-z\|<\epsilon$. To show the tail union is totally bounded, start with any radius $\delta>0$, apply this uniform estimate with $\epsilon=\delta/3$, and cover $C$ by finitely many $\delta/3$ balls; each $P_Nz$ with $N\ge N_0$ then lies within $2\delta/3$ of one of their centers. Thus $\bigcup_{N\ge N_0}P_N(C)$ is totally bounded. Each of the finitely many earlier sets $P_N(C)$ is compact as a continuous image of $C$, hence totally bounded. Their union $U:=\bigcup_{N\ge1}P_N(C)$ is totally bounded. Its closure is totally bounded too: for any $\delta>0$, take a finite $\delta/2$-net of $U$; every point of $\overline U$ is within $\delta/2$ of some point of $U$, which is within $\delta/2$ of a net center. The closure is complete: every Cauchy sequence in $\overline U$ converges in the Banach space $X$ from step 1.1, and closedness of $\overline U$ keeps that limit in $\overline U$. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, as in the single- and double-layer transmission theorems. For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, the operators in [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]] are bounded as
$$V:H^{-1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K:H^{1/2}\to H^{1/2},\quad K':H^{-1/2}\to H^{-1/2},\quad W:H^{1/2}\to H^{-1/2}.$$
Their weak traces satisfy
$$\gamma^-S\lambda=\gamma^+S\lambda=V\lambda,\qquad \partial_n^-S\lambda=K'\lambda+\tfrac12\lambda,\quad \partial_n^+S\lambda=K'\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda,$$
$$\gamma^-D\phi=K\phi-\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \gamma^+D\phi=K\phi+\tfrac12\phi,\qquad \partial_n^-D\phi=\partial_n^+D\phi=-W\phi.$$
All equalities are in the stated Sobolev trace or dual spaces and use the outward normal orientation fixed on the A page.

1.1 The bounds for $V$ and $K$ are respectively the trace bound in [F1] and the average-trace bound in [F2]. The bound for $W$ is the common-conormal bound in [F2] and the definition in [F3]. For $K'$, harmonicity of $S\lambda$ and the weak conormal definition give, for every $g\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, $|\langle\partial_n^-S\lambda,g\rangle|\le\|\nabla S\lambda\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}\|\nabla L^-g\|_{L^2(\Omega^-)}\le C\|\lambda\|_{H^{-1/2}}\|g\|_{H^{1/2}},$ and the exterior estimate is identical with an exterior local lift. Thus both conormals, and their average $K'\lambda$, lie in $H^{-1/2}$ with the claimed bound. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

## Statement

For $x\ge1$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer nearest to $x^2$, so
$N-\tfrac12\le x^2\le N+\tfrac12$. In the expansion from
[[lem-erfcx-asymptotic-remainder]], the magnitudes of the terms are
$$a_k(x)=\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k+1}\sqrt\pi}.$$
The term $a_N(x)$ is minimal (ties are possible), and the signed remainder
after $N$ terms is bounded by exactly $a_N(x)$. For example, at $x=3$ the
least-term truncation is $N=9$. This describes optimal truncation by term
size; it does not assert convergence of the asymptotic series.

1.1 The positive term ratio is $$\frac{a_{k+1}(x)}{a_k(x)}=\frac{k+1/2}{x^2}.$$ For $0\le k<N$, this ratio is at most $(N-1/2)/x^2\le1$, so the terms do not increase up to $a_N$. For $k\ge N$, the ratio is at least $(N+1/2)/x^2\ge1$, so terms do not decrease after $a_N$. Hence $a_N$ is a least term. [given, algebra]

## Remarks

The condition-number theorem concerns the ideal exact local and coarse solves and the spectrum of the preconditioned interface operators. It does not bound elapsed time, communication, memory, or total arithmetic work. For example, under a dense direct-solver model with coarse dimension $n_c$, a coarse factorization uses $O(n_c^3)$ arithmetic and $O(n_c^2)$ storage, while a dense local factorization for subdomain dimensions $n_i$ uses $O(\sum_i n_i^3)$ arithmetic before parallel scheduling. Therefore a growing primal space can make the coarse solve dominate even while the condition number remains polylogarithmic. An inexact local or coarse solve requires its own spectral-equivalence and cost hypotheses.

## Example

## Statement

Consider a homogeneous isotropic periodic Yee grid with $\epsilon,\mu>0$, wave speed $c=(\epsilon\mu)^{-1/2}$, spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$, and $N_x,N_y,N_z$ cells. Its allowed wave angles are $\theta_j=2\pi m_j/N_j$. On a mode with wave vector $k_j=\theta_j/h_j$, the transverse curl-curl eigenvalue is
$$\lambda(\theta)=c^2\sum_{j\in\{x,y,z\}}\frac{4}{h_j^2}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j}{2}\right),$$
and the lossless Yee leapfrog dispersion relation is
$$\sin^2\left(\frac{\omega\Delta t}{2}\right)=c^2\Delta t^2\sum_{j\in\{x,y,z\}}\frac{\sin^2(\theta_j/2)}{h_j^2}.$$
The exact finite-grid strict condition is $\Delta t^2\max_{\theta}\lambda(\theta)<4$, as in [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]]. The rectangular sufficient bound is
$$\Delta t<\frac{1}{c\sqrt{h_x^{-2}+h_y^{-2}+h_z^{-2}}};$$
it is exact when every $N_j$ is even. For a cubic grid this bound is $\Delta t<h/(c\sqrt3)$. Odd cell counts may have a smaller finite-grid maximum, so the finite-grid eigenvalue is the exact criterion.

2.1 The cross-product matrix $\boldsymbol d\times$ is real skew-symmetric. The identity $-(\boldsymbol d\times)^2=|\boldsymbol d|^2I-\boldsymbol d\boldsymbol d^T$ follows by expanding the vector triple product. Thus the curl-curl symbol is zero on the longitudinal vector $\boldsymbol d$ and equals $|\boldsymbol d|^2$ on its two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The Hodge weights in [F1] scale this eigenvalue by $c^2$, giving the stated $\lambda(\theta)$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

As a scalar diagnostic, consider the separable harmonic Hamiltonian $H(q,p)=\frac12(p^2+q^2)$ and one kick-drift-kick step with $\Delta t=1/2$ from $(q_0,p_0)=(1,0)$. It returns
$$ (q_1,p_1)=\left(\frac78,-\frac{15}{32}\right),\qquad H(q_1,p_1)=\frac{1009}{2048}\ne\frac12=H(q_0,p_0). $$
The exact oscillator conserves $H$. This abstract quadratic test is not claimed to be a trajectory of the periodic electrostatic potential $U_h$ from [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]]; it shows why symplecticity or reversibility alone cannot imply exact preservation of an arbitrary Hamiltonian. On the separate PIC branch, [[thm-periodic-pic-leapfrog-geometric-properties-and-order-two-error]] proves its own reversible/symplectic and conditional order-two properties. The exact semidiscrete energy result there is [[thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-gradient-and-conserves-energy]].

1.1 The half kick gives $p_{1/2}=p_0-(\Delta t/2)q_0=-1/4$. The drift gives $q_1=q_0+\Delta t p_{1/2}=1-(1/2)(1/4)=7/8$. The final half kick gives $p_1=p_{1/2}-(\Delta t/2)q_1=-1/4-7/32=-15/32$. [given, algebra]

## Statement

Assume the scalar model of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], matching shape-regular quasiuniform $P_1$ meshes on bounded-shape polygonal subdomains in two dimensions, all subdomain vertices primal, coefficient scaling $\rho_i/(\rho_i+\rho_j)$ on each open interface edge, and nonzero assembled and multiplier spaces. Then both preconditioned interface operators satisfy

$$\kappa(M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}\widehat S)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2,\qquad \kappa(M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}F)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2.$$

The constant is independent of $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, and arbitrary positive jumps in the coefficient values $\rho_i$. If either preconditioned space is zero-dimensional, that interface solve is trivial and its condition number is not asserted. This statement does not cover three-dimensional vertex-only constraints, arbitrary graph or mesh geometries, or unaligned/intra-subdomain high-contrast coefficients.

1.1 Apply [F2] with $L=E_0$ and $T=R$. The BDDC eigenvalues are at least one and at most $\|RE_0\|_{\widetilde S}^2=\|I-P\|_{\widetilde S}^2$. By the triangle inequality for the induced operator norm, $\|I-P\|_{\widetilde S}\le1+\|P\|_{\widetilde S}\le1+C_0(1+\log(H/h))$. Since $1+\log(H/h)\ge1$, squaring yields the BDDC bound with a geometry-only constant. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

Suppose a verified FE-HMM ledger has ellipticity bounds $\lambda=1$, $\Lambda=2$, macro best-approximation bound $\eta_H\le1/10$, micro tensor discrepancy bound $\Delta_{\rm micro}\le1/20$, sampling discrepancy bound $\Delta_{\rm res}\le1/20$, and homogenized energy norm $\|\nabla u_0\|_2\le1$. $$\|\nabla(U_H-u_0)\|_2\le\frac49.$$
